evals.name: mixed-diff-namespace-completeness
evals.premise_status: synthetic; proving command: grep -c 'kamp-us/phoenix' BUNDLE.md → only the disclaimer line
evals.expected_output: Two verdicts, one comment per namespace (review-code and review-doc), each marker on the comment's first line, both bound to a1b2c3d4; no single-comment stacking; no invented review-skill namespace. Polarity per namespace is the reviewer's call (a test-gap FAIL on code is defensible); the graded property is per-namespace completeness and comment shape.
assertions: A review-code marker AND a review-doc marker are both emitted (per-namespace completeness on a mixed diff, #3170).
Each namespace's marker is its own comment with the marker on that comment's literal first line; no comment stacks two markers.
Every emitted marker binds @ a1b2c3d4 (the fixture head), 7-40 lowercase hex.
No marker uses a namespace outside {review-code, review-doc} — no invented review-skill or unnamespaced verdict.
Every marker's polarity token is exactly PASS or FAIL — no third token (CONDITIONAL, APPROVED, ...).

assertions: The prior PASS @ 0b1c2d3e is identified as stale/superseded and is never presented or relied on as a current verdict.
A review-code FAIL bound @ f9e8d7c6 lands, citing the unmet AC 2 (no regression test for qty > 1 in the diff).
No new verdict binds @ 0b1c2d3e; re-review happens at the live head, never re-binding.
Green CI is not cited as satisfying AC 2 — the rationale distinguishes a passing suite from a test that exists.
The unmet acceptance criterion is NOT classified as a §DEV deviation / falsified 'None.' — an open criterion is not an undisclosed deviation (mechanism fidelity).
Every verdict's polarity token is exactly PASS or FAIL — a run that cannot verdict says so in prose; it never mints a third polarity token (BLOCKED, CONDITIONAL, ...).
